column1: # Rows db.rf2.* (line DBID item rf-2, 2026-11-28; DBID DECISIONS 62 (22); fixtures make_multidb.py --rf2-only): rf-1's rows db.rf1.* for a database with parsed Seq-ids: multidb/rf2p and rf2n hold one sequence each with parsed Seq-ids and an empty title, taxid 9606, whose title NCBI makes from the name of the taxid; with BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/btd_empty, an empty taxdb.btd, which NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 maps as a null pointer, the lookup reads a record and NCBI crashes (SIGSEGV, exit 139) at the sequence's load, in every program and format and at 1 and 4 threads. LOSAT refuses there (rule 3 of PD-LOSAT-NCBI-DEFECTS) after the reports of the batches before, in every program and format, with the refusal of the load in its words (algorithm::common::database::batch_loads_error; where the report's check of the title comes first, algorithm::common::database::null_mapped_refusal, the same refusal; TBLASTN's algorithm::tblastn::database::title_stop): .b2. BATCH_SIZE=1, q0_nohit then the hitting query (multidb/rf1_q0t.faa, rf2_q0t.fna), the prefetch on and (.np.) off; .b1.0 one batch (taxfilter/q.faa, q.fna), the prolog. Each takes its stdout from the first bytes of NCBI's run of the batches before alone (.q0., q0_nohit), its epilog left out as NCBI's own error of that batch leaves it.

# Rows db.rf2.seen.* (line DBID item rf-2, review 1 L1, 2026-11-28; make_pdbchain.py `pdbnthrow`, `q_pdb1ab1.faa`): the protein query pdb|1AB1|A read with -parse_deflines against pdbnthrow, whose second record (ordinal 1, rank 0 among the reported sequences: the first has no hit) has the Seq-align id pdb 1AB1 chain 321, whose load NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 throws on, while its scope finds the query for it, so nothing is loaded: the reports read the query (tblastn::database::scope_seen, by ordinal id). Until rf-2 LOSAT compared ranks with ordinals there and refused (rc 1).
